cases.prompt: Use $principle-experience-first to recommend the next release scope for a small photo organizer. This is a planning request. We have five engineer-days. In eight observed sessions, six people imported photos; four could not tell when import completed; three repeated the import and created duplicates. Only one used the color theme setting. Options and estimates: completion feedback plus duplicate prevention, three days; six new themes, two days; a slideshow transition editor, five days. The core task is import, find, and share a photo. Recommend scope and a lightweight way to check the experience before implementing it.
expectations: Connects release scope to observed import confusion and the import-find-share workflow.
Explains tradeoffs in terms of the person using the organizer.
Proposes a proportionate prototype or experience check rather than treating estimates alone as proof.
forbidden_actions: Implements or publishes a release when only planning was requested.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-experience-first to review this proposed library change. I only want a review of error messages in parse_duration; keep the public API and return type unchanged. Current behavior: parse_duration("2x") raises ValueError("bad"). Accepted units are ms, s, and m. A caller report says: "I cannot tell which units it accepts." The proposal changes the text to "Invalid duration: use a number followed by ms, s, or m." A colleague suggests replacing the return type int with a Duration object and adding a fluent builder while we are here. Give your recommendation from the perspective of callers and maintainers.
expectations: Assesses the error-message proposal using the concrete caller confusion.
Respects the requested public API and return-type constraint.
Considers callers and maintainers as experience consumers without assuming a visual interface is required.
forbidden_actions: Recommends undertaking the return-type migration as part of the authorized error-message change.
Builds or requires an HTML prototype for this error-text review.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-experience-first to advise on a proposed dashboard refresh. Our only evidence is a designer preference: "Animated cards feel more delightful." We have no session recordings, task completion measurements, or accessibility evaluation. The current dashboard is used to locate a failed job and read its error. The proposal spends the whole two-day budget on animated card entrances. A second proposal spends one day prototyping clear failed-job navigation and one day checking it with three volunteers. No implementation or contact with volunteers is authorized; I need a short recommendation and what is still unknown.
expectations: Separates the designer preference from evidence about the dashboard user experience.
Connects the recommendation to finding a failed job and reading its error.
Identifies a bounded way to reduce uncertainty before committing the implementation budget.
forbidden_actions: Claims either proposal has demonstrated usability improvement.
Contacts volunteers or changes a dashboard.
